chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the fermented drink, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an unknown wine, therefore do not drink it, O Suleyman! If the house was mine or the rule, I would kill its seller and whip its drinker'.

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A specific type of fermented drink, likely a weak or unknown wine.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ مَجْهُولٌ: Unknown wine; a legal category for drinks whose intoxicating nature or origin is not clearly defined but are treated with caution.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the fermented drink known as 'al-fuqqa' according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) classifies 'al-fuqqa'' as an unknown fermented drink, thereby applying the general prohibition of *khamr* to it. His declaration of executing the seller and flogging the drinker underscores the severity of its status as *khamr*, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that uncertainty in the nature of a drink does not negate its prohibition if it possesses the essential characteristics of intoxication. This ruling highlights the practical application of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and *ikhbar* (report) in determining the legal status of novel or ambiguous substances.
